name: Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology
short_description: Develop Your Automotive Skills. Drive Your Career Forward.
description: Build practical automotive knowledge and technical skills with the Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology. Learn to inspect, service, diagnose and repair a wide range of light vehicle systems, including engines, brakes, steering, suspension and automotive electrical components.

overview.heading: Build Your Future in the Automotive Industry
overview.description: The AUR30620 Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology is designed for individuals seeking to develop the technical knowledge and practical skills required to work in the automotive service and repair industry.
content: This qualification covers a broad range of automotive activities, including vehicle servicing, engine diagnostics, electrical systems, braking systems, steering, suspension and mechanical repairs.

You will develop the ability to identify vehicle faults, perform diagnostic procedures, use automotive tools and equipment, and carry out repairs in accordance with workplace safety and industry standards.

Whether you are starting your automotive career or looking to have your existing mechanical experience formally recognised, this qualification can support your professional development in the light vehicle automotive sector.

why_choose.heading: Why Choose This Qualification?
why_choose.description: Develop industry-relevant automotive skills, build practical mechanical capabilities and prepare for opportunities across the automotive service and repair industry.

benefits.title: Develop Practical Mechanical Skills

overview.heading: Develop Skills to Support and Empower Others
overview.description: The CHC51015 Diploma of Counselling is designed for individuals seeking to develop the knowledge and skills required to work in supported counselling roles within established agencies and community service organisations.
content: This qualification develops skills in counselling communication, interviewing, establishing professional relationships, understanding personality and development theories, applying counselling therapies and supporting clients through decision-making processes.
Learners also develop an understanding of ethical practice, professional boundaries, diversity, case management and reflective professional development.
The qualification prepares individuals for defined counselling roles within appropriate organisational structures and does not represent preparation for unrestricted independent counselling practice.

career_pathways.heading: Career Pathways
career_pathways.description: This qualification can support career opportunities across bookkeeping, accounts administration, payroll and financial support roles.

items.title: Bookkeeper
items.description: Maintain financial records, process transactions and manage bookkeeping activities.

items.title: Accounts Officer
items.description: Assist with accounts payable, accounts receivable and financial administration.

items.title: Payroll Officer
items.description: Process payroll, employee payments and payroll records.

items.title: Accounts Administrator
items.description: Support daily financial and administrative operations.

items.title: Financial Accounts Assistant
items.description: Assist with financial reporting and accounting activities.

items.title: BAS Agent
items.description: Provide eligible BAS services after obtaining the required Tax Practitioners Board registration.

items.title: Assistant Accountant
items.description: Support financial reporting, reconciliations and accounting functions.

items.title: Accounting Clerk
items.description: Maintain financial documentation and assist with accounting operations.
